主要内容: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that median weekly earnings for full-time wage and salary workers in the second quarter of 2013 were $776, representing a 0.6 percent increase compared to the same period in 2012. This growth was lower than the 1.4 percent increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers over the same period. The data, which is not seasonally adjusted, showed that women who usually worked full time had median weekly earnings of $707, or 82.2 percent of the $860 median for men. The women's-to-men's earnings ratio varied by race and ethnicity, with white women earning 81.1 percent as much as their male counterparts, compared to black women (91.6 percent), Asian women (77.1 percent), and Hispanic women (94.2 percent). Among major race and ethnicity groups, black men working full-time had median weekly earnings of $666, or 75.3 percent of the median for white men ($885). Overall, median weekly earnings for Hispanics who worked full time ($572) were lower than those of blacks ($634), whites ($799), and Asians ($973).
